primary_source_R20_verified.citation: P. Gopalan, P. G. Kolaitis, E. Maneva, C. H. Papadimitriou, 'The Connectivity of Boolean Satisfiability: Computational and Structural Dichotomies,' SIAM J. Comput. 38(6):2330-2355, 2009 (ICALP 2006; arXiv cs/0609072).
primary_source_R20_verified.definition_6_tight: A set S of relations is TIGHT iff at least one holds: (1) every relation is componentwise bijunctive; (2) every relation is OR-free; (3) every relation is NAND-free.
primary_source_R20_verified.theorem_10_diameter: If S is tight, then for every CNF(S)-formula the diameter of the solution graph G(phi) is LINEAR in the number of variables; otherwise there exist CNF(S)-formulas whose G(phi) has diameter EXPONENTIAL in n (2^Omega(sqrt n)).
primary_source_R20_verified.section_4: If S is Schaefer, then S is tight (the converse fails).
primary_source_R20_verified.jurisdiction: BOOLEAN domain only. G(phi) connects solutions at Hamming distance 1. The dichotomy is about (a) st-connectivity complexity and (b) component DIAMETER — NOT about the pairwise-overlap dispersion this instrument measures, and NOT about |D|>2.
primary_source_R20_verified.load_bearing_consequence: All Boolean census families (Horn, dual-Horn, bijunctive, affine, and their 0/1-valid sub-cases) are Schaefer -> TIGHT -> the SAME bin (linear component-diameter). GKMP's dichotomy therefore does NOT force the affine-vs-bounded ruggedness ORDERING this instrument measures — they are all tight. The instrument's ordering is a FINER distinction than GKMP draws.

successor_literature_check_timeboxed.result: EMPTY for the domain-3 rows. The Reconfiguration-CSP (single-flip) connectivity dichotomy is Boolean (Gopalan et al.; follow-ups arXiv 1403.6165, 1510.06700). For non-Boolean / larger domains there is NO published solution-space connectivity dichotomy — 'notoriously hard,' 'not studied'; still an OPEN, active direction as of 2025 (arXiv 2511.22914, 'Towards an algebraic approach to the reconfiguration CSP').
successor_literature_check_timeboxed.consequence: the domain-3 census rows (order-3, median-3, lin-eq-z3, lin-eq-z3-b) are OUTSIDE any published connectivity classification's jurisdiction — theory-silent by pre-committed absence.

per_family_theory_netting_column._legend: theory-forced = a published classification (or field-agnostic linear algebra) DETERMINES the terrain class; theory-permitted = consistent with the classification but the quantitative reading is not forced; theory-silent = outside every published classification's jurisdiction.

xor-sat.basis: GKMP tight (linear diameter) + solution set is a coset of a GF(2) linear subspace; random linear-code coset -> pairwise Hamming concentrates ~ n/2 -> low overlap / dispersion is FORCED by linear algebra.

zerovalid-affine.basis: as xor-sat (homogeneous GF(2) coset; dispersion forced).

onevalid-affine.basis: as xor-sat (affine GF(2) coset; dispersion forced).

lin-eq-z3.basis: coset of a GF(3) linear subspace; dispersion forced by linear algebra (field-agnostic). NB GKMP-proper is Boolean-silent here; the FORCING is the coset argument, not GKMP.

horn-sat.basis: GKMP tight (Schaefer); Horn relations closed under min -> solution set is a distributive lattice, single-flip-connected, concentrated toward the least model -> consensus/clustering (smooth) forced by order theory + GKMP.

dual-horn.basis: dual of Horn (closed under max); lattice, connected, smooth forced.

zerovalid-horn.basis: 0-valid Horn; still min-closed lattice -> smooth forced.

2-sat.basis: GKMP tight (bijunctive = median-closed -> CONNECTED, linear diameter) — connectivity forced, but the QUANTITATIVE mid-level overlap this instrument reads is NOT forced by the diameter class. Consistent with, not forced by, GKMP.

zerovalid-bijunctive.basis: 0-valid bijunctive; GKMP tight/connected forced, overlap degree not forced.

order-3.basis: |D|=3 semilattice (min) CSP. GKMP is Boolean-only; NO published non-Boolean connectivity dichotomy; not affine (no coset argument). Terrain class is outside every published classification's jurisdiction. THE ANOMALY ROW.

median-3.basis: |D|=3 majority/median CSP. As order-3: Boolean-silent, non-affine, no published |D|=3 connectivity result. THE ANOMALY ROW.

jurisdiction_fact_on_record: The anomaly rows (order-3, median-3) are domain-3 and theory-SILENT. If the anomaly (bounded-width yet affine-rugged) SURVIVES the fresh confirmation draws, it does so as a measurement NO published classification speaks to — the strongest novelty position available, established here by PRE-COMMITTED ABSENCE, not discovered at writeup.

three_tier_writeup_scoring_rule.rule: H_I6b's confirmed ordering (if it lands) is reported in three tiers; NO tier borrows another's language.
three_tier_writeup_scoring_rule.theory_forced_tier: the theory-forced portion (affine dispersion; Horn/dual-Horn lattice-consensus) is reported as MEASURED CONFIRMATION of known structure theory — valuable, NOT novel.
three_tier_writeup_scoring_rule.theory_permitted_tier: the theory-permitted portion (bijunctive quantitative overlap) is reported as QUANTITATIVE REFINEMENT beyond what theory forces.
three_tier_writeup_scoring_rule.theory_silent_tier: the theory-silent portion (the domain-3 order-3/median-3 anomaly, IF it holds on fresh data) is reported as the NOVEL MEASURED FINDING — no published classification addresses it.
